q: How does a listed company report BRSR value chain emissions when an MSME supplier gives no data?
title: Value chain BRSR when a supplier is silent
short: Report what partners actually sent, state the coverage you reached, and either leave silent suppliers out with that gap named or add a clearly labelled estimate with its method. Never fold estimates into partner-reported totals without saying so. The disclosure is voluntary from FY 2025-26, so partial, clearly stated coverage is a legitimate answer.

sections.h: Who is on the partner list
p: The list is set by value. Since SEBI's March 2025 circular, a supplier or customer is a value chain partner if it alone is 2% or more of your purchases or sales, and you may stop adding partners once those covered reach 75%. For the top 250 listed companies the whole disclosure is voluntary from FY 2025-26, and its assessment or assurance is voluntary from FY 2026-27.

sections.h: Three ways to handle a silent supplier
ol: Make it easy to answer: send a one-page template with only the indicators you need, the April to March period and the units, and offer a call. Many MSMEs can work out Scope 1 and 2 from a year of fuel invoices and electricity bills once they know what is wanted.
Disclose with coverage: report the partners that responded and state their share of purchases. Name the gap rather than hide it.

Estimate, clearly labelled: from the supplier's own proxies, such as known output or sanctioned load, from the intensity of responding peers making similar goods, or from a spend-based factor. Show the method and the data used.

sections.h: How estimates fit the GHG Protocol
p: SEBI asks for the BRSR Core indicators of each partner to the extent they are attributable to your business with that partner. Chapter 7 of the GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard allows secondary data and estimates where primary data is not available, provided the method and data quality are disclosed. A reader of the BRSR value chain section expects figures supplied by partners, so keep estimates on a separate line or in a footnote and never present them as partner data.
Agree with your assessment or assurance provider, before the season, how estimates should be shown.

sections.h: What to keep for the assessor
ul: The partner list with each partner's share of purchases or sales.
Responses as received, with the factor sources the partner gave.
For each estimate: method, inputs, source and date.

example.title: Worked example: coverage and one estimate
lines: Annual purchases: Rs 3,000 crore; suppliers at 2% or more: 10, together Rs 2,160 crore (72%)
7 responded, covering Rs 1,500 crore: 50% of purchases, and 1,500 / 2,160 = 69% of the partner group
Silent supplier: Rs 90 crore of your purchases (3%)
Two responding suppliers of similar castings report 1.8 and 2.2 t CO2 per crore of revenue; average 2.0 (illustrative)
Estimate attributable to your purchases: 90 x 2.0 = 180 t CO2, shown separately as a peer-intensity estimate
example.note: SEBI asks for the share attributable to your business with the partner, so scale a partner's whole footprint by your share of its sales, and do it the same way for every partner.

senseible: A supplier using Senseible can build its Scope 1 and 2 from its own fuel invoices and electricity bills and share the totals with factor sources; where only spend exists, Senseible provides a spend-based estimate labelled with wider uncertainty. How estimates appear in the BRSR is the listed company's decision.
